title: Place and order whole numbers, fractions and decimals together on a number line

lesson.title: Putting Everything on One Number Line

steps.say: You already know how to compare fractions with different bottom numbers, and how to line up decimals like zero point two five and zero point three. Today we do one small thing with all of that: putting whole numbers, fractions, and decimals together on the same number line, so you can see which one is biggest.

visual.caption: One line, and everybody gets a spot on it

steps.say: Here is the trick. A number line does not care what a number looks like. It only cares how far along the line it sits. Think of the walking path at the beach with markers every metre. Zero point five metres, one half of a metre, and half a metre are all the exact same spot. So when you meet a mixed group of numbers, ask each one the same question: how far along am I?

visual.caption: Zero point five and one half land on the very same dot

steps.say: Let's try a real one. At the school fun run, Maya ran zero point seven five kilometres, Ben ran one half of a kilometre, and Sofia ran one whole kilometre. I will place them on a line from zero to one. One half sits right in the middle. Zero point seven five sits three quarters of the way, so it is past the middle. One is at the very end of the line.

visual.caption: Ben at one half, then Maya at zero point seven five

steps.say: Now read the line from left to right, and you have your order. One half is smallest, then zero point seven five, then one. So Ben ran the shortest distance, Maya was in the middle, and Sofia ran the farthest. Notice how easy that was once every number had a dot.

visual.caption: Left is always smaller, right is always bigger

steps.say: Here are two traps I want you to watch out for. Some kids think zero point two five is bigger than zero point three because it has more digits. But on the line, zero point two five sits before zero point three, so it is actually smaller. Longer does not mean bigger. The same kind of trap happens with fractions: one eighth is not bigger than one quarter, even though eight is bigger than four. When you cut a granola bar into eight pieces, each piece is tinier. On the line, one eighth sits closer to zero than one quarter does.

visual.caption: Zero point two five really does come before zero point three

steps.say: So whenever you get a messy mix of whole numbers, fractions, and decimals, do not argue about which one looks bigger. Just draw one number line and give every number its dot. The line always tells the truth.

lesson.answer: Put every number on the same number line, then read left to right — the line always tells you the order.

practice.question: Three friends measured how much water they drank at soccer practice. Ayla drank three quarters of a litre, Noah drank zero point four litres, and Priya drank one whole litre. Draw a number line from zero to one, mark all three amounts on it, and then write the three amounts in order from smallest to largest.
practice.answer: Zero point four comes first, then three quarters (which is zero point seven five), then one. So the order is: Noah with zero point four litres, Ayla with three quarters of a litre, Priya with one litre.
